label: Mid/late original-phase input of e/b/l/s/h/z/y/d/m/0
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.5% of mass), at positions 3-7 (peak t=4-5, near the end of the input); never at t=0, essentially never on <DEL> or during copy. Within that window it is selective for the current input token: e, b, l, s, h, z most strongly (rate 13-18%), then y, d, m, 0. It prefers first occurrences of a token (in_first lift 1.6x). Magnitude is highest when h (and to a lesser degree x) appeared earlier in the prefix: top examples all have h/x early, and prev_tok=h / prev2_tok=h have about 3.7x lift. The position-plus-token-set predicate gets about 0.78 of mass but precision is only about 0.4. The remaining dependence looks like a graded mix of current token and prefix content that a boolean rule does not capture cleanly.
